_comment: chatgpt_search_mix — ES mapping for the new ChatGPT Ads network (platform 21). Modeled on google_ads_data_v2.mapping.json's PROVEN, already-tuned-in-production conventions, not invented from scratch: (1) FLAT field names, no facebook-style 'table.field' dotted prefixes — this network has no legacy PHP payload shape to stay compatible with, and flat keys avoid the whole readPath()/dotted-vs-nested ambiguity class of bug seen elsewhere in this codebase. (2) dynamic:false so an unexpected payload key never triggers ES's default dynamic-mapping (which is how the google index ended up with runaway auto-ngram fields). (3) keyword+lowercase_normalizer for every exact-match/filter field (term/terms queries — cheap) instead of wildcard-able text fields. (4) text+content_analyzer (standard tokenizer, no edge_ngram, no stemming) only on the handful of fields that genuinely need full-text search. (5) index:false on every display-only field (raw source URLs, NAS display paths that are never filtered/sorted on) to save both index size and CPU. (6) number_of_shards is LOW (2) because this is a brand-new, zero-document index — google's own index needed 4 shards only after growing to 206M docs/219GB; over-sharding an empty index wastes resources and slows aggregations for no benefit. Re-shard (reindex into a new index with more shards) only if/when real volume justifies it.

properties._comment_dates: all three are written as 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' by esDocBuilder.coerceEsDate, matching every other network's search_mix convention.
properties._comment_filters: exact-code filters -> keyword+normalizer (term/terms in filter context = cheapest ES query shape).
properties._comment_content: Genuinely free-text ad copy only. match(AND)/match_phrase at query time, never wildcard — wildcard on a text field is the CPU trap being avoided here.
properties._comment_owner: word-match (text) + .kw for exact/prefix/sort/aggregation, same split google_ads_data_v2 uses.
properties._comment_urls: URLs: keyword, no analyzer, no edge_ngram.
properties._comment_media: NAS paths that the displayable-media gate needs `exists`/`wildcard(*DefaultImage*)` on stay indexed. Everything purely for display (raw source URLs, video/carousel paths nothing ever filters on) is index:false — saves space and CPU, matches google_ads_data_v2's own split.
